papers.title: A human-like EEG signature of cognitive control in the domestic dog.
papers.abstract: In humans, theta (θ) band activity (defined as 4-8 or 5-7 Hz), measured over the frontal midline of the scalp, is an important EEG correlate of voluntary and conscious self-control. Theta waves recorded over the frontal lobes can therefore implicate neocortical control mechanisms. Other likely physiological markers include alpha and beta power, and more recently, a flattened 1/f slope. In the domestic dog, inhibitory self-control is extensively studied, but mostly through behavioural tests. Here, we present a first inquiry into possible EEG correlates of cognitive control in family dogs by comparing short (~ 30-second-long) EEG recordings from two conditions: passive wakefulness (baseline) versus a delayed gratification challenge (test). These conditions were recorded in a random sequence within the same session, under overall identical settings. In total, we collected 226 short recordings from fourteen dogs. We observed an increase in neural activity (test > baseline) that resembles human cognitive theta in frequency range (4-8 Hz) and which is similarly more pronounced over the frontal midline. Another important finding is a reduction in broadband power and the flattening of the spectrum, which implicates the work of fronto-parietal connections. While these markers do not differentiate between different facets of cognitive control, our capacity to measure them in awake dogs sets the stage for further EEG-based inquiries into canine cognition.

papers.title: Hypothalamic astrocytes fine-tune the signals governing metabolism.
papers.abstract: Astrocytes are known to have key roles in the neuroendocrine control of metabolism. The spectrum of actions of this cell population continues to expand as their heterogeneity is deciphered and new study approaches are employed. Astrocytes were first implicated in metabolic control when they were shown to participate in hypothalamic inflammation induced by high-fat diets, which leads to complications such as continued weight gain and glucose intolerance. In addition to their participation in pathophysiological processes associated with poor nutrition and obesity, these glial cells are now accepted as fundamental players in the physiological control of energy homeostasis. Along with their effect on neurons controlling appetite and energy expenditure, glial cells are implicitly involved in the generation of circadian rhythms, including eating and sleep patterns that affect metabolism and may link metabolism with other neuroendocrine systems such as puberty. The evolving concepts regarding astrocytes in metabolic control, including their participation in responses to currently used obesity drugs, highlight them as potential therapeutic targets. Here, we review advances in our understanding of how astrocytes participate in these processes, describe the mechanisms involved and discuss future directions.

papers.title: Winter awakening routine for attenuating the morning blood pressure surge.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular events cluster in the early morning and peak in winter, when the morning blood pressure surge is accentuated by cold. The Japanese Society of Hypertension has identified the winter morning as a critical window in which cold stress, awakening-related sympathetic activation, physical activity, and arising from bed converge, and has recommended gentle activity such as light stretching and deep breathing on waking, without specifying its content. For a national public broadcaster, under the Society's supervision, we designed a 2-minute routine to be performed in bed after awakening: five slow, deep breaths combined with a whole-body stretch, slow rolling from side to side, ankle circles and ankle pumps, followed by sitting up in stages on the bed and five shoulder-blade lifts combined with slow, deep breathing and gentle neck extension before standing. We describe the physiological rationale for each element, drawing on evidence that the morning rise in blood pressure is related mainly to arising rather than awakening, that slow breathing enhances baroreflex sensitivity, that neck posture modulates carotid sinus input, that the blood pressure response to physical activity predicts the morning surge and is heightened in winter and older age, and that orthostatic hypertension is linked to the surge. The routine is intended to make the rise from the sleep trough to the standing morning blood pressure slower and smoother, and thereby to lower the morning peak. Future studies using ambulatory blood pressure monitoring on winter mornings are needed to test whether the routine attenuates the morning surge.

papers.title: Toward patient-centered blood pressure monitoring: validation of a novel low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method according to the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 standard.
papers.abstract: Out-of-office blood pressure (BP) measurement is central to contemporary hypertension management. However, conventional oscillometric BP monitors often require substantial cuff inflation, potentially causing discomfort, sleep disturbance, and reduced adherence to repeated BP measurement. We developed a novel low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method designed to reduce the cuff pressure and measurement duration while maintaining accuracy. Here, we evaluated the novel automated upper-arm BP monitor incorporating this method (i.e., the Omron HEM-7290T) according to the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 standard. The device was assessed in 85 adults using the ISO same-arm sequential measurement protocol. Reference BP values were obtained by simultaneous auscultation. The device's performance was evaluated according to Criteria 1 and 2 of the ISO standard. For Criterion 1, the mean device-observer differences were 0.5 ± 7.09 mmHg for systolic BP (SBP) and 0.6 ± 5.50 mmHg for diastolic BP (DBP). For Criterion 2, the standard deviations of the subject-level mean differences were 5.79 mmHg for SBP and 5.05 mmHg for DBP. All results fulfilled the ISO 81060-2:2018/Amd1:2020/Amd2:2024 validation requirements across the required BP and arm circumference distributions. The Omron HEM-7290T successfully fulfilled ISO validation requirements in adults with 20- to 45-cm arm circumferences. These findings demonstrate that a low-pressure and rapid oscillometric method can achieve international-standard accuracy while potentially reducing the measurement burden. This study provides the clinical validation of a patient-centered BP monitoring technology designed to improve comfort without compromising performance, with potential applications in home BP monitoring, nocturnal BP assessment, and digital hypertension management.

papers.title: Using error-related brain activity to identify mismatches during virtually simulated and electrically stimulated upper-limb movements.
papers.abstract: Patients recovering from motor impairments can benefit from rehabilitation therapy provided using functional electrical stimulation (FES). Yet, its clinical adoption has been limited, due to poor repeatability and inconsistencies in performance. To overcome these challenges, several closed-loop techniques have been proposed that rely on position or force sensors. The use of additional sensors not only increases the device's weight and cost, but it is also difficult to deploy in a clinical environment. Studies involving EEG report error-related potentials (ErrPs) that occur when a person perceives a mismatch or error in their own actions or that of others. This study investigates whether we can detect movement errors when using FES. Two experimental paradigms are presented: one generates errors during discrete stepwise movements, while other generates errors during continuous or sweeping motion of the upper arm. Within the continuous movement experiment, ErrPs arise when observing movement of a virtual Avatar's arm or when using electrical stimulation. Using an ensemble classifier based on decision trees, ErrPs could be successfully detected with an accuracy of 96 ± 3% for discrete and 91 ± 13% for continuous movement errors, respectively. This study demonstrates that ErrPs arise even for errors generated by a rehabilitation device like FES, paving the way for a feedback controller FES using ErrPs.

papers.title: During natural vision, semantic novelty modulates fixation-related processing in primate cortex.
papers.abstract: We sample visual scenes with short gaze fixations separated by saccades. While low-level integration is known, semantic integration of foveal vision across fixations remains unclear. We hypothesized that the brain responds to changes in semantic information from one fixation to the next, and therefore postulated a neural signal associated with semantic novelty for each saccade. Novelty was measured from different layers of a deep network on foveal vision. Only semantic, and not low- or mid-level, novelty modulated frontal and occipital fixation-related potentials in male and female human scalp EEG during natural viewing of full-length movies (3.4x106 saccades). Intracranial recordings in male and female humans (9.0x104 saccades) and female non-human primates (Macaca mulatta; 3.3x104 saccades) revealed broadband high-frequency activity modulations in scene-specific ventral visual and frontal brain areas only for semantic novelty. This modulation was stronger for movies than static images, and frontal modulation occurred early alongside occipital modulation, suggesting top-down effects. This modulation of fixation-related activity with novelty suggests that foveal representations are compared between consecutive fixations to construct scene representations during natural viewing in primates.Significance statement Primate vision relies on eye movements to sample the world, yet how the brain integrates high-level meaning across these "snapshots" remains a mystery. By combining deep-learning models with massive electrophysiological datasets from humans and macaques, we show that the brain responds to changes in semantic content between fixations, but not low- or mid-level changes. We identified a "semantic novelty" signal that modulates neural activity across the primate cortex. These findings suggest visual processing is not a series of independent glimpses, but a continuous process comparing consecutive foveal information at the semantic level. This work bridges biological vision and artificial intelligence, providing a new framework for understanding how the brain maintains a coherent understanding of a dynamic world.

papers.title: Persistent Severe OSA Despite Ongoing CPAP Therapy.
papers.abstract: A 51-year-old man was referred to our sleep medicine clinic for reevaluation of previously diagnosed OSA. The diagnosis had been established approximately 4 years earlier, at a body weight of 105 kg (BMI, 31.7 kg/m2). At that time, cardiorespiratory polygraphy documented severe OSA, with an apnea-hypopnea index of 97 events/h. Mean nocturnal oxygen saturation (Spo2) was 91%, and the cumulative time spent with Spo2 < 90% accounted for 38% of the total recording time, indicating a substantial nocturnal hypoxemic burden. Nocturnal CPAP therapy had been prescribed, delivered through an oronasal mask at a fixed pressure of 11 cm H2O.

papers.title: Simultaneous dynamic spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare earth elements in acidic chloride media using response-specific multivariate calibration.
papers.abstract: Reliable spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare-earth elements in strongly acidic chloride media remains analytically challenging because of weak 4f-4f absorption responses, severe spectral overlap, and baseline instability under dynamic measurement conditions. This study presents a dynamic absorption spectroscopic method coupled with a response-specific multi-scale peak-basis linear regression model (RS-MPBLR) for continuous in situ quantification of Nd3+ and Pr3+ in strongly acidic coexisting systems relevant to NdFeB magnet recycling. Characteristic absorption peaks, multi-scale spectral descriptors, and derivative-related features were integrated to enhance response specificity and robustness against spectral overlap, acidity-dependent background variation, and flow-induced baseline drift. Spectral analysis confirmed an approximately linear absorbance-concentration relationship within the investigated range, supporting peak-oriented linear modeling. RS-MPBLR was evaluated using leave-one-concentration-out cross-validation and benchmarked against partial least squares, principal component regression, and ridge regression, achieving lower prediction errors and more stable error distributions. Dynamic online experiments demonstrated continuous tracking of stepwise concentration changes, with R2 values above 0.97 and limits of detection of 0.07 and 0.03 g/L for Nd3+ and Pr3+, respectively. Cross-day segment-wise analysis further confirmed stable online predictions, with coefficients of variation mostly below 1-2% and σpred values within 0.015-0.040 g/L for Nd3+ and 0.006-0.021 g/L for Pr3+. This study provides a robust and sensitive spectrophotometric soft-sensing strategy for continuous rare-earth ion quantification in hydrochloric acid media. By combining response-specific modeling with reference-sample-based calibration correction, it overcomes the difficulty of long-term dynamic detection under online flowing conditions and enables reliable quantification for NdFeB magnet hydrometallurgical recycling.

US real-world data: sleep and mental health burden in chronic spontaneous urticaria.
papers.abstract: Sleep and mental health (MH) impacts have been understudied in chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU); there is a lack of large, real-world cohort studies in the United States (US). To describe the proportion of patients with claims for sleep and MH conditions, including health care resource utilization (HCRU), before (baseline) and after (follow-up) CSU diagnosis, and among patients with controlled vs uncontrolled CSU. Adults (≥18 years) with CSU in the US HealthVerity claims database were included (January 2016-October 2023). Prespecified proxy events identified patients with uncontrolled CSU (any CSU-related inpatient [IP], emergency department [ED], or urgent care visit or any use of systemic corticosteroids, biologics, or immunosuppressants during follow-up). Claims for sleep-related conditions (insomnia, sleep-wake disorders), MH conditions (anxiety, chronic fatigue, depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, somatic symptoms, and related disorders), sleep aids/antidepressants, and sleep and MH-related HCRU (outpatient, IP, and ED visits) were examined. Overall, 224,958 patients were included (mean follow-up: 2.4 years). The proportion of patients with claims for sleep-related conditions increased from baseline to follow-up (8.8% vs 15.4%), and for MH conditions (40.6% vs 56.3%). In total 113,932 patients (50.6%) experienced uncontrolled CSU; a higher proportion of patients with uncontrolled vs controlled disease had ≥1 claim for sleep-related (17.3% and 13.4%) and MH conditions (60.6% and 51.9%). Sleep and MH-related HCRU increased after CSU diagnosis and was greater among patients with uncontrolled vs controlled disease. Claims for sleep-related and MH conditions increased after CSU diagnosis, particularly among patients with uncontrolled disease, highlighting the need for more effective management.

papers.title: Broadband gamma-band EEG changes during magnetophosphene-inducing 20 Hz magnetic field stimulation.
papers.abstract: Magnetophosphenes are visual percepts induced by extremely low-frequency magnetic fields (ELF-MF; <300 Hz), yet the EEG expression of suprathreshold magnetophosphene-inducing stimulation remains poorly characterized and is not reliably captured by classical low-frequency markers. We tested whether suprathreshold 20 Hz tAMS is accompanied by broadband high-frequency EEG changes rather than focal oscillatory effects. EEG was recorded in N=13 healthy volunteers during 20 Hz sinusoidal magnetic-field exposure delivered using transcranial alternating magnetic stimulation (tAMS) in a global-head configuration. Three conditions were analyzed: no exposure (0 mT), subthreshold (5 mT), and suprathreshold (50 mT). Gamma-band EEG power (30-80 Hz) was quantified using complementary spectral approaches, including aperiodic-adjusted gamma power. Perception reports sharply dissociated the three conditions, with frequent perception at 50 mT only. Suprathreshold stimulation was associated with spatially distributed increases in gamma-band EEG power over frontal and occipito-parietal electrodes. The differences remained partly detectable in complementary analyses using two local aperiodic-adjustment methods and did not exhibit a consistent narrowband peak, a pattern consistent with broadband high-frequency changes. No focal power change over primary occipital electrodes remained significant after Bonferroni correction. These findings identify a spatially distributed broadband high-frequency scalp EEG effect associated with the suprathreshold 50 mT condition, with the main spatial pattern strongly preserved after ICA-based removal of components classified as ocular or muscular. The effect therefore characterizes the coupled suprathreshold stimulation-perception condition; its perception specificity and physiological source remain unresolved.

papers.title: 'A shadow of her former self': The mental and physical health impacts of temporary accommodation for homeless neurodivergent children and their families in the United Kingdom.
papers.abstract: This article provides the first dedicated analysis of the mental and physical health impacts of temporary accommodation (TA) on homeless neurodivergent children in the UK. While TA is formally designated as short-term housing, families frequently experience prolonged stays, repeated forced moves, and accommodation that is unsafe, overcrowded and poorly regulated. Drawing on a 2025 UK-wide call for evidence co-designed with parents and frontline practitioners, the paper offers empirically novel insights into how these conditions generate distinctive and intensified harms for neurodivergent children and their families. Using a rigorous thematic analysis of 280 qualitative responses, the study demonstrates how sensory overload, chronic unpredictability, spatial confinement and environmental hazards exacerbate existing health conditions, and are reported to contribute to developmental regression, disrupted sleep, malnutrition, and emotional dysregulation. Elevated risks of self-harm and injury, which can even necessitate family separation, were also identified. Crucially, the findings frame TA as a whole-family relational health crisis with cascading effects across households, including siblings and parents - many of whom are themselves neurodivergent. By newly centring neurodivergent children and their families as a primary analytic group, the article addresses a critical epistemic gap in homelessness, housing, and child health research, which has marginalised neurodiversity within the study of child homelessness.

papers.title: Clinical features and outcomes in children with late-onset febrile seizures.
papers.abstract: Late-onset febrile seizures (LFS), occurring at or after five years of age, are uncommon and may represent a heterogeneous clinical group. We aimed to characterize their clinical, EEG, neuroimaging, and short-term outcome features and to compare de novo and persistent LFS subgroups. This retrospective, single-center study included 119 children with fever-associated seizures at or after 60 months of age. De novo LFS was defined by no febrile seizure history before five years, whereas persistent LFS was defined by one or more earlier febrile seizures. Clinical characteristics, EEG and brain MRI findings, antiseizure medication (ASM) use, and incident epilepsy after the index event were evaluated. Seventy children (58.9%) presented at 60-83 months, and 93 (78.2%) had seizures lasting <5 min. Forty-four children had de novo LFS and 75 had persistent LFS. EEG was performed in 104 children: 82 (78.8%) were normal, 20 showed background slowing, and 2 showed focal epileptiform discharges. Brain MRI was performed in 66 children; 63 were normal and 3 showed incidental findings, with no potentially epileptogenic lesion identified. During 12-36 months of follow-up, 10 children (8.4%) were diagnosed with incident epilepsy, all in the persistent LFS subgroup (10/75 vs. 0/44); eight of these cases fulfilled the ILAE practical definition of epilepsy. Most LFS were brief and had generally favorable short-term outcomes. All incident epilepsy cases occurred in children with febrile seizures before five years of age; however, given the small number of outcomes and overlapping confidence intervals, this observation is hypothesis-generating and does not permit reliable subgroup-specific risk estimation. Larger prospective studies with standardized assessments and longer follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Automated intracranial spike analysis across sleep-wake states localizes the seizure onset zone in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are an established biomarker of epilepsy, but their utility for seizure-onset zone (SOZ) localization has been limited by reliance on short recording samples, research-grade detectors, and a primary focus on spike frequency. We assessed multi-day intracranial IED activity across sleep-wake states and its ability to localize the SOZ in adults and children. We analyzed simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG data from 17 patients in the EPILEPSIAE database (predominantly adult) and 10 pediatric patients at the Alberta Children's Hospital (ACH), with 48 to 72 h of data per patient. FDA-cleared clinical software (Persyst P15a) performed automated sleep staging and IED detection. We introduced a novel IED activity metric reflecting IED amplitude and the relative consistency of channel participation across detected events and used logistic regression with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation to predict SOZ channels for each sleep-wake state. IED activity was significantly higher in SOZ than in non-SOZ channels across every sleep-wake state in both cohorts. N2 sleep yielded the highest AUROC for SOZ localization (0.69 EPILEPSIAE; 0.77 ACH), but differences across states were not statistically significant. The presence of clinical seizures during the recording did not significantly affect localization performance. Automated intracranial IED analysis localizes the SOZ in adults and children, with only modest variation across sleep-wake states. Amplitude-aware IED analysis using clinically deployed software is a practical adjunct to presurgical SOZ localization. The modest effect of sleep-wake states suggests that clinical value can be obtained without state-specific analysis. This approach may strengthen presurgical evaluation in adult and pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy.

papers.title: Hidden ordered frequencies in disordered magnetic systems: An inverse analysis of µSR spectra.
papers.abstract: Strong magnetic disorder can suppress observable muon-spin precession, making it difficult to distinguish genuinely disordered magnetic states from magnetic states containing characteristic internal-field contributions masked by random-field broadening. We introduce Convolution-Constrained Inverse $\mu$SR Analysis (CCI-$\mu$SR), a framework combining zero-field (ZF) and transverse-field (TF) measurements to investigate potentially hidden characteristic internal-field contributions. Disorder-induced broadeninginferred from model-based ZF analysis is incorporated as a constraint in TF fitting, restricting the range of admissible local-field descriptions. We demonstrate the approach using the pyrochlore iridate Y$_{1.8}$Cu$_{0.1}$Ca$_{0.1}$Ir$_2$O$_7$, where strongdamping obscures coherent oscillations. Conventional Fourier analysis does not resolve a distinct internal-field frequency, while unconstrained Prony reconstruction yields model-dependent estimates. The CCI-$\mu$SR framework provides a physicallyconstrained description compatible with a strongly broadened quasistatic magnetic component. Profile-$\chi^2$ analysis supports a finite characteristic internal-field frequency in ZF within the adopted model. The complementary TF analysis demonstrates that a strongly broadened finite-frequency contribution remains compatible with the measured response, even when it cannot be independently resolved or uniquely distinguished from a zero-frequency alternative. These findings highlight the ability of CCI-$\mu$SR to assess potentially hidden magnetic contributions through jointly constrained ZF and TF descriptions, while explicitly identifying the limitations of frequency reconstruction.

papers.title: Biobehavioral correlates of perceived health-related quality of life in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: Toward an extended framework for understanding health impact.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated central nervous system disorder; relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) is the most common form. Self-perceived health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has been linked to psycho-behavioral and immunological factors, but their interplay remains unclear. We examined psycho-behavioral, clinical, and immunological correlates of perceived physical and mental health. In this cross-sectional study, 85 patients with RRMS (78% female; mean age 40.6 ± 10.3 years; predominantly mild disability) were assessed for fatigue, sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, anxiety/depression symptoms, and perceived cognitive dysfunction. Blood samples were analyzed for complete blood counts and, in a subgroup, lymphocyte subpopulations; the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) was calculated. HRQoL was measured using the SF-36 Physical and Mental Component Summaries (PCS and MCS). Hierarchical linear regression models included sociodemographic, clinical, and treatment-class covariates, with sensitivity analyses. Disability, fatigue, and depressive symptoms were associated with lower PCS, and sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms with lower MCS. Higher lymphocyte count was associated with higher MCS (β = +0.268, p = 0.006; ΔR2 = 0.030), consistently across all four sensitivity analyses. SII was not significantly associated with either outcome. In exploratory flow-cytometry analyses (n = 33-34), NK cells were associated with PCS (β = +0.345, p = 0.003), but not significantly with MCS. HRQoL in RRMS showed psychological and clinical associations, with an additional lymphocyte-MCS association. The clinical relevance of the immune findings, including the exploratory NK-PCS association, requires further investigation.

papers.title: A digital cognitive battery for sleep-disordered breathing: Test-retest reliability and practice effects.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects cognitive performance and may contribute to long-term cognitive decline. Longitudinal assessments are needed for measuring changes in cognitive functioning in relation to OSA progression and treatment. This requires standardized, reliable cognitive assessments suitable for repeated use, but the psychometric properties of cognitive tests may vary across populations. We evaluated the suitability of a digital cognitive battery, covering various cognitive functions, for repeated administration in individuals with varying OSA severity, based on its psychometric properties. The battery included 14 cognitive tasks. We assessed test-retest reliability, practice effects, and ceiling and floor effects between two administrations (mean interval 12 weeks) in 46 participants (mean age = 49 ± 16 years, 21 women) with a wide range of OSA severity (mean apnea-hypopnea-index (AHI) = 17.6 ± 17.7). Psychometric properties varied considerably between cognitive tasks. Test-retest reliability estimates were good or satisfactory (ICC≥.60) for the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT), Symbol Digit Modalities Task (SDMT), Paced Auditory Serial Addition Task (PASAT), Auditory Verbal Learning Task (AVLT), and subscores of the Tower of London Task (ToL). Practice effects were high for the PASAT in Level 1 (p<.001,r=.63) and the Inspection Time Task (ITT; p<.001,r=.52). Ceiling effects were present in the ITT and ToL, whereas intrusions in the AVLT and lapses in the PVT occurred infrequently and clustered at the lower bound. Only a subset of cognitive tasks showed adequate psychometrics for repeated administration, highlighting the need for careful task selection and modification when developing cognitive assessments for repeated application in OSA populations. We include recommendations on cognitive test selection and test design for repeated assessments in OSA populations.

papers.title: A sex-specific modification of the SARA questionnaire for obstructive sleep apnea screening: Comparative validation against six other tools in the HypnoLaus cohort.
papers.abstract: and objectivesObstructive sleep apnea is significantly underdiagnosed in women, partly because existing screening tools were developed in male-predominant cohorts and may fail to capture female-specific clinical presentations. We used the HypnoLaus population-based cohort (n = 1540; 718 women, 822 men) to evaluate seven OSA screening tools in this cross-sectional study and assessed whether adding menopausal status to SARA enhances diagnostic accuracy. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as AHI ≥ 15 events per hour on polysomnography. The study included 1540 participants (718 women, 822 men). NoSAS and the updated SARA demonstrated the highest overall discriminative performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), 0.741 (95% CI, 0.718-0.764) and 0.693 (95% CI, 0.669-0.716), respectively, followed by original SARA (AUC, 0.684), Berlin (0.635), SONA (0.579), STOP-Bang (0.575), and ESS (0.507). Incorporation of menopausal status improved discrimination of SARA in women (AUC 0.675 vs. 0.627; p = 0.001). Although NoSAS showed the highest overall AUC, updated SARA performed more consistently across sex-, age-, and BMI-defined phenotypes. In women ≤55 years, updated SARA showed higher discrimination than NoSAS (AUC 0.616 vs. 0.509; p = 0.014), and in lean women (BMI <25 kg/m2), updated SARA detected cases that NoSAS missed (sensitivity 42.3% vs. 0%). Sex-related differences affect OSA screening. Incorporating menopausal status into SARA improved OSA detection in women. At the same time, anthropometry-weighted tools such as NoSAS performed poorly in younger, leaner women, underscoring the limitations of anthropometry-based screening in these phenotypes.

papers.title: Sex-related clinical profiles in obstructive sleep apnea: An integrated clinical, sleep study, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy analysis.
papers.abstract: Sex-related differences in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are well recognized, but their association with dynamic upper airway collapse remains poorly characterized. To characterize sex-related clinical profiles in OSA through the integrated assessment of clinical characteristics, sleep study parameters, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) findings. This retrospective study compared clinical profiles, sleep parameters, collapse patterns, airway reversibility, and treatment recommendations in 767 patients undergoing DISE. Women were older and more frequently reported insomnia and mood disorders, whereas men had higher body mass index, larger tonsils, and higher Mallampati scores. Sleep study differences were also observed: men exhibited longer apneas, higher apnea-to-hypopnea ratios, and more positional OSA. Respiratory event clustering suggestive of REM-related OSA was more frequent in women, although REM sleep was not EEG-confirmed. DISE demonstrated that obstruction was more frequent in men at all assessed levels, including palatal concentric collapse (62.5% vs 40.7%). Complete resolution with jaw thrust was more frequent in women (30.2% vs 18.4%). Mandibular advancement therapy was more commonly recommended for women, whereas surgery was more frequently recommended for men. Findings in this DISE-selected cohort suggest a predominantly anatomy-driven pattern in men and a potentially more functionally modulated profile in women, supporting the integration of sex-related characteristics into personalized treatment selection.

papers.title: Serial Amplitude-Integrated Electroencephalography and the Burdjalov Score in Preterm Infants: A Prospective Longitudinal Bedside Study in the Neonatal Care Unit.
papers.abstract: Preterm birth interrupts occurs during a critical period of cortical organization, and objective bedside tools for tracking functional maturation remain limited. The aim of this study was to assess the interobserver reproducibility of the Burdjalov score and to characterize longitudinal electrocortical maturation in preterm infants up to term-equivalent age. Prospective longitudinal observational study in a neonatal intensive care unit and an intermediate care unit, data collected from September 2021 to August 2023. Infants born before 35 weeks of gestation, stratified by gestational age (GA) at birth (<28, 28-30, 31-34 weeks), who underwent serial two-channel amplitude-integrated electroencephalography until term-equivalent age or discharge. Term newborns with a single recording served as physiological reference. Outcomes measures were the Burdjalov scores, rated independently by three blinded observers was. Agreement was assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient and kappa, maturation by linear regression on corrected GA, and time to a maximal score of 13 by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Forty-eight preterm infants (125 recordings) and 29 term newborns were included. Total-score agreement was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.98, 95% confidence interval 0.98-0.99), with kappa ≥0.60 for all components. Scores rose continuously with corrected GA in all strata, approaching maximal values around 37 weeks and matching the term reference. Time to maturity did not differ between strata (log-rank P = 0.823). Serial amplitude-integrated electroencephalography scored with the Burdjalov scale is an objective, highly reproducible method for monitoring electrocortical maturation in preterm infants. Functional maturation follows corrected age rather than GA at birth, providing a bedside reference for detecting atypical maturational trajectories.

papers.title: Temporal coherence between metoceanic variability and green turtle nesting phenology in the Mexican Atlantic.
papers.abstract: Ecological traits of sea turtles are strongly influenced by their environment, making these species highly sensitive to climatic variability, particularly under global oceanic and atmospheric changes. Assessing the relationships between environmental variability and sea turtle phenology is critical for understanding potential population responses under climate change and informing adaptive management at critical habitats. We assessed the nesting phenology of Chelonia mydas across three beaches in the Mexican Atlantic (Isla Aguada, Lechuguillas, and Tamul), representing contrasting oceanographic conditions. We used long-term nesting data (2009-2023), to examine temporal coherence between nesting activity and sea surface temperature (SST) and a spatially accumulated precipitation indicator using cross-spectral analyses. The nesting season began in June (eight-day intervals 23-31) and ended in early October across all sites, and its duration averaged 12 ± 0.8 eight-day intervals. Cross-spectral analyses revealed consistent annual coherence between nesting activity and both environmental variables, with SST signals preceding nesting activity by up to approximately 3.9 weeks and precipitation signals by up to 5.3 weeks. These relationships varied among sites and represent temporal associations rather than evidence of direct causation. Our results highlight the relevance of short-term metoceanic variability to nesting phenology within a broader context of interacting environmental and reproductive processes. Integrating phenological indicators with environmental observations can support climate-informed monitoring, improve operational planning, and inform adaptive conservation strategies under future climate scenarios and support climate-informed monitoring and conservation planning.

papers.title: Imagery-based fear conditioning and extinction learning in individuals with psychotic liability: an EEG study.
papers.abstract: Pavlovian fear conditioning using aversive imagery rather than physical stimuli as the unconditioned stimulus (US) provides a powerful paradigm to study fear learning in psychosis, in which threat expectations often develop in the absence of proximal external threats. This preregistered study aimed to identify behavioral, psychophysiological, and neural aberrancies in imagery-based fear acquisition and extinction learning associated with psychotic liability. Participants at-risk for psychosis (n = 70 with elevated psychosis proneness, n = 28 with verified clinical high-risk status) and non-clinical controls (n = 55) underwent an imagery-based fear conditioning paradigm. Participants learnt to produce aversive, neutral (US), or no imagery in response to cues (shapes) that were systematically paired with a different neutral face (conditioned stimulus; CS). Behavioral ratings, EEG (late positive potential; LPP), and psychophysiological responses (skin conductance responses; SCRs) were assessed. The at-risk group showed more pronounced acquisition learning in fear and arousal ratings and LPPs than controls. This pattern was driven by elevated affect ratings to the CS+ that had been paired with aversive imagery. In contrast, explicit expectancy ratings indicated less CS discrimination in at-risk individuals. The at-risk group also showed reduced extinction learning in expectancy but faster extinction learning in fear and arousal ratings than controls. Psychotic liability is associated with an increased susceptibility to acquire fear through negative mental imagery, even in the absence of actual threat. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of psychosis, suggesting that imagined threat beliefs could contribute to delusion formation.

papers.title: From driving (L0) to living (L5): Intergenerational car comfort concept by Etic-emic theory.
papers.abstract: This study explores intergenerational vehicle comfort using the Etic-Emic framework, translating a psychological concept into automotive guidelines. A scoping review identified 34 parameters, and trend analysis of 1789 Scopus articles (1953-2025) tracing comfort across vehicle generations. Expert interviews with 15 specialists classified them as Etic (relevant to L0 and L5) or Emic (emerging specifically in L5), suggesting additional factors. Group brainstorming refined classifications, yielding 44 parameters, including factors such as brand identity and cargo space. Safety, vibration control, and fuel efficiency were stable Etic parameters, whereas non-driving tasks, confidence to sleep or fully recline, legal liability transparency, and cybersecurity were Emic. The novel "Intergenerational Car Comfort" concept provides OEMs an actionable decision tool: its Etic-Emic matrix guides trade-offs, including safety constraints versus expectations to recline and sleep. Ultimately, it identifies legacy architectures to retain or those requiring new interior packaging and HMI solutions, providing a roadmap for next-generation automated vehicles.

papers.title: Patient-level EEG seizure classification with AHCNet: Hybrid CNN and handcrafted feature fusion.
papers.abstract: Automated seizure classification from electroencephalography (EEG) necessitates rigorous validation, particularly concerning patient independence and potential dataset biases. This study evaluated hybrid feature fusion and confidence-based deferral for patient-level EEG classification. We assembled a class-balanced cohort of 198 patients from the Temple University Hospital seizure and epilepsy corpora, including individuals with focal non-specific seizures, generalized non-specific seizures, or no epilepsy. Our approach combined a multiscale one-dimensional convolutional neural network with handcrafted spectro-temporal and inter-channel spatial features. We assessed its performance using nested patient-level cross-validation and metadata-only baselines. Stacking and feature-fusion models achieved accuracies of 78.8% (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 73.2-84.3%) and 78.3% (72.2-83.8%), respectively, showing no statistically significant difference. Notably, segment-level validation inflated accuracy by 20-23 percentage points. Metadata alone yielded 72.2% accuracy, and complete confounding between corpus origin and control-versus-seizure status precluded attributing this distinction solely to EEG content. Among 132 seizure patients from the same corpus, a two-class focal-versus-generalized classification achieved 81.1% accuracy, significantly outperforming metadata alone (at most 59.8%). Spatial features enhanced accuracy by 2.0-8.1 percentage points across models. While confidence weighting did not improve accuracy, deferring the 20% least-confident patients increased accuracy among the retained patients from 78.8% to 84.8%. These findings underscore the critical importance of patient-level validation and thorough confounding assessment when evaluating hybrid EEG classifiers. This framework is still investigational. For clinical application, it requires controls drawn from the same corpus as seizure cases and external validation.

papers.title: Technology and Intelligence: Staying on Target for the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy for deep-tissue biophysical stimulation: an integrated clinical and molecular analysis.
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders such as osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, radicular syndromes, and osteoporosis require noninvasive treatments reaching deep anatomical structures. Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy (NMRT/MBST) delivers depth-independent resonance-based stimulation. This systematic review consolidates clinical and mechanistic evidence to evaluate NMRT/MBST among deep-tissue biophysical therapeutics. A systematic search of PubMed, Ovid/Embase, and peer-reviewed literature identified 26 original studies spanning randomized and observational clinical evidence, imaging evaluations, veterinary trials, and in vitro research. Experimental findings on inflammatory, metabolic, mitochondrial, redox, and circadian pathways were integrated with clinical observations. NMRT/MBST shows a strong safety profile with no reported treatment-emergent adverse events. Across indications, studies demonstrate improvements in pain, function, and, selectively, structural or densitometric changes. Mechanistic evidence indicates modulation of mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, inflammatory cascades, chondrogenic and osteogenic pathways, neurotrophic activity, and circadian regulation. These convergent processes mirror photobiomodulation, supporting NMRT/MBST as a deep-acting analog influencing regenerative biology in inaccessible tissues. Conventional pulsed electromagnetic field therapy is physically the closest comparator but shows narrower mechanistic overlap. Evidence remains heterogeneous in methodology, outcome measures, and structural responses. The only placebo-controlled knee osteoarthritis trial found no superiority over sham, although baseline imbalance limits interpretation. The depth-independent profile and mechanistic parallels suggest applications in deep cartilage, subchondral bone, intervertebral discs, and nerve-root environments, supporting multimodal biophysical strategies. Priorities include larger randomized trials, longitudinal structural evaluation, comparisons with optical modalities, and biomarker-guided personalization.

papers.title: Deep Sedation in Single-Shot Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Head-to-Head Look at Two Pulsed Field Versus Cryoballoon Ablation Approaches.
papers.abstract: Deep sedation (DS) is routinely used during single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) to optimize patient comfort and procedural stability. However, data on sedative requirements and procedural tolerance of pulsed field ablation (PFA) under DS compared with thermal technologies remain limited. In this single-center study, consecutive patients underwent PVI with cryoballoon (CB), PFA using a pentaspline catheter (PC) or the balloon-in-basket catheter (BC). All procedures were performed under DS with midazolam, fentanyl, and propofol, administered by electrophysiology staff without anaesthesiologist supervision. Propensity score matching (1:1:1) was applied for age, sex, body mass index, and hypertension. Procedural characteristics, sedative/analgesic requirements, and complications were analyzed. Acute PVI without major complications was achieved in all 156 enrolled patients. PC procedures were associated with higher body-weight- and time-adjusted requirements for propofol (CB: 0.10 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; PC: 0.15 ± 0.04 mg/kg/min; BC: 0.11 ± 0.03 mg/kg/min; p < 0.001) despite the lowest total dose of propofol used (CB: 440 ± 144 mg; PC: 348± 80 mg; BC: 433 ± 160 mg; p = 0.00). Procedural times (CB: 47.5 [40-60] min, PC: 29 [25-35] min, BC: 47.5 [40-56] min, p < 0.001) and fluoroscopy times (CB: 9.5 [6.3-13.6] min; PC: 6.2 [4.4-9] min; BC: 7.2 [6.1-11.2] min, p = 0.001) were shortest in the PC group. Sedation-related hemodynamic stability was comparable across all cohorts. The novel BC demonstrated excellent feasibility under DS, with reduced normalized sedative requirements compared with the PC and a safety profile comparable to CB ablation. These findings suggest that optimized waveform design and field homogeneity may enable safe and comfortable PVI under DS without the need for general anesthesia.

papers.title: Advanced Two-Stage Authentication with EEG: Inter-Subject P300 ERP Classification Using EEGNet for User Recognition.
papers.abstract: A reliable biometric system is crucial in modern security challenges. EEG signals offer a promising alternative to conventional biometrics due to their uniqueness, forgery resistance, and long-term stability. Among EEG-based approaches, P300 event-related potentials (ERPs) are widely studied for their robustness in distinguishing individuals. This study proposes a two-stage authentication framework integrating user identification (multi-class classification) and authentication (binary classification) for enhanced security. A comprehensive EEG preprocessing pipeline including bandpass filtering, epoch rejection, temporal cropping, and downsampling was implemented to improve signal quality and extract cleaner P300 responses. EEGNet, a lightweight convolutional neural network designed for EEG analysis, was used for feature extraction and classification. 16 participants across three sessions evaluated the system robustness under cross-session conditions. The framework demonstrated strong generalization, achieving up to 95% precision and a mean accuracy of 96.10% for both identification and authentication. These results highlight the potential of EEGNet user authentication using P300 ERPs, offering insights into optimal preprocessing and deep learning methods for EEG-based security. This study underscores brainwave-driven authentication as a secure and viable alternative to traditional biometrics, paving the way for real-time applications in cybersecurity and identity verification.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: Comparison of quality of life between docetaxel and weekly paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant treatment of breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Taxane-based chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment for stage II-III breast cancer. Weekly paclitaxel and 3-weekly docetaxel exhibit comparable oncologic efficacy but differ in toxicity profiles and treatment schedules. This study aimed to compare longitudinal patient-reported quality-of-life (QoL) outcomes between these two taxane regimens. This single-center observational cohort study included 82 patients with stage II-III breast cancer who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy followed by either docetaxel every 3 weeks (n=55) or weekly paclitaxel (n=27). QoL was assessed at four time points using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B), Beck Anxiety Inventory, Beck Depression Inventory, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and Quality of Life Enjoyment and Satisfaction Questionnaire. Longitudinal changes and between-group differences were also analyzed. Baseline QoL scores were comparable between groups. During active treatment, both regimens were associated with deterioration in several QoL domains, with recovery observed following treatment completion. At the third assessment time point, corresponding to peak treatment burden, patients receiving docetaxel reported significantly higher depressive symptoms and lower life satisfaction compared with those receiving weekly paclitaxel. However, global FACT-B scores or sleep quality showed no significant differences at any time point. Hematologic adverse events, particularly anemia and neutropenia, were more frequent in the docetaxel group, whereas peripheral sensory neuropathy was more common with weekly paclitaxel. No grade 4 adverse events or treatment-related deaths occurred. Weekly paclitaxel and 3-weekly docetaxel yielded broadly comparable longitudinal QoL outcomes in curative-intent breast cancer treatment. Docetaxel was associated with a greater short-term psychological burden during peak chemotherapy exposure. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating patient-reported outcomes into treatment selection and supportive care strategies.

papers.title: Psychiatric symptoms were not associated with obstructive sleep apnea severity in a Japanese working population.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity and psychiatric symptoms, including depression, anxiety, insomnia, and excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life, in a Japanese working population. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 707 municipal employees in Japan who participated in the Night in Japan Home Sleep Monitoring study. OSA severity was assessed using the respiratory event index (REI) obtained from home sleep apnea testing and categorized as none, mild, and moderate-to-severe. Psychiatric symptoms were evaluated using validated questionnaires: the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, Athens Insomnia Scale, and Japanese version of Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, and occupational factors. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed. Among the 707 participants (mean age 44.8 years ± 11.5 years; 58.0% female), 263 (37.2%) had OSA, including 171 (24.2%) with mild OSA and 92 (13.0%) with moderate-to-severe OSA. After adjustment, OSA severity was not associated with insomnia, depression, anxiety, or excessive daytime sleepiness. No significant differences in quality-of-life scores were observed across OSA severity groups. In this working population, objectively measured OSA severity was not significantly associated with most psychiatric symptoms or quality of life. These findings suggest that OSA severity alone may not adequately reflect the aspects of sleep disturbance most relevant to mental health in this Japanese working population. UMIN-CTR (UMIN000028675, August 15, 2017) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03276585, August 3, 2017).

papers.title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Core Symptoms and Sleep Disturbances in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: This meta-analysis was designed to determine whether transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) confers measurable benefits for selected behavioral features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for sleep problems in pediatric ASD populations. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across eight electronic databases-PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, CBM, VIP, and Wanfang-covering the period from each database's inception through June 1, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The methodological quality of the included trials was appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias assessment instrument. Quantitative synthesis was performed with RevMan 5.4 and Stata 17.0, following the PRISMA statement for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Ultimately, seven studies qualified for inclusion in this systematic review. Pooled analyses showed that tDCS was associated with lower ATEC scores (mean difference [MD] = -8.81, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -12.06 to -5.56, p < 0.00001), ABC scores (MD = -12.08, 95% CI: -21.75 to -2.41, p = 0.01), and CSHQ scores (MD = -4.95, 95% CI: -8.66 to -1.24, p = 0.009). However, no statistically significant difference was observed for CARS scores (MD = -1.12, 95% CI: -4.15 to 1.91, p = 0.47). tDCS, most commonly delivered at 1 mA over the DLPFC, was associated with improvements in some ASD-related behavioral outcomes; preliminary evidence also suggested a potential benefit for sleep disturbances, although this finding was based on only two low-certainty studies and warrants cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Research Summary.
Orforglipron for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Results From 2 Randomized Clinical Trials (ATTAIN-OSA).
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common disorder characterized by repeated upper airway collapse during sleep that is associated with reduced quality of life and increased incidence of cardiometabolic disease. To assess the effects of orforglipron on moderate to severe OSA in adults with obesity or overweight, compared with placebo. Two 52-week, phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials were conducted at 66 sites in the US, Argentina, Brazil, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Japan, Mexico, and Taiwan. Adults with moderate to severe OSA and body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) of 27 or higher were enrolled between November 11, 2024, and July 23, 2025. Final follow-up occurred on July 30, 2026. Trial 1 included patients not receiving positive airway pressure treatment and trial 2 included patients receiving positive airway pressure treatment. Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either once-daily orforglipron (maximum tolerated dose: equivalent to 9-, 14.5-, or 17.2-mg tablet dose) or placebo. The primary end point was change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, events/h) from baseline to week 52. Seven key multiplicity-controlled secondary end points included change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Short Form Sleep-Related Impairment T-score, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. A total of 363 patients were randomized in trial 1 (mean age, 48.4 years; BMI, 37.4; AHI, 50.7 events/h; 31.4% female) and 349 patients were randomized in trial 2 (mean age, 51.1 years; BMI, 38.6; AHI, 57.6 events/h; 26.9% female). For the treatment regimen estimand, in trial 1, the mean AHI change was -17.8 for orforglipron compared with -4.5 for placebo (difference, -13.2 [95% CI, -17.7 to -8.7]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. In trial 2, the mean AHI change was -17.3 for orforglipron and -5.3 for placebo (difference, -12.0 [95% CI, -17.1 to -6.9]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. Of 7 key secondary end points, 6 were statistically significant, favoring orforglipron. Gastrointestinal events were the most commonly reported adverse events, occurring in 123 (68.0%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 68 (37.4%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 1 and in 125 (70.6%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 63 (36.6%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 2. These results provide evidence for the potential use of oral orforglipron to improve sleep-disordered breathing in adults with moderate to severe OSA and obesity or overweight. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06649045.

papers.title: Time-dependent efficacy of vitamin D3 against chronic stress-induced behavioral and circadian deficits via the hepatic VDR-clock axis.
papers.abstract: Vitamin D3 (VitD3) is an essential fat-soluble micronutrient that protects against chronic stress-related disorders through its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects. Major depressive disorder is accompanied by circadian rhythm (CR) disruption, and evidence from chrono-nutrition studies suggests that nutrient effects are strongly influenced by administration timing. However, whether VitD3 efficacy against chronic stress depends on intervention timing remains unclear. This study assessed the chrono-nutrition potential of VitD3 in a mouse model of chronic stress. Mice subjected to 4 weeks of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) received daily VitD3 either in the morning (AM) or evening (PM). VitD3 treatment mitigated CUMS-induced behavioral impairments, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage in a time-dependent manner, with superior outcomes observed with PM administration. PM administration enhanced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, hippocampal integrity, TNF-α levels, sleep duration, and serotonin synthesis. Mechanistically, PM administration more effectively restored hepatic Vdr rhythmic oscillation, coupled with re-synchronization of the core clock network. Genetic validation in Caenorhabditis elegans further supported the essential role of VDR in circadian restoration. This study is the first to reveal the time-dependent antidepressant effects of VitD3 and identify the VDR-circadian clock axis as the underlying mechanism. These findings highlight the importance of intervention timing for VitD3 efficacy and support precision nutrition strategies aligned with CR for stress disorders.

papers.title: Clinical features of the postictal state in adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.abstract: Persons with epilepsy may experience many postictal symptoms after a seizure, which can significantly impact quality of life. We aimed to determine the frequency, duration, and severity of postictal symptoms to better characterize the postictal period. Our cross-sectional questionnaire was adapted from a prior pediatric postictal survey. Face and content validity were evaluated by epilepsy experts and patients from the Calgary Epilepsy Program (CEP). The survey was pilot tested and modified, consisting of 14 physical, cognitive, and psychiatric postictal signs and symptoms. Consecutive CEP adults who had agreed to participate in research and experienced a seizure in the prior 2 years were approached. CEP clinical data were used to supplement survey data. Frequency of factors alleviating and exacerbating postictal symptoms were examined. Spearman's rho was used to explore associations between survey and CEP registry data with statistical significance at ≤ 0.05. Of 351 patients approached, 313 agreed to participate (89%). Fourteen were lost after consent was obtained, and 15 were excluded (incomplete surveys, missing registry data, not having epilepsy). Of the 298 final participants, 54% were female, mean age was 40 years (SD = 15.6), and 95% (282/298) experienced at least one postictal symptom. The three most frequent postictal symptoms were fatigue, sleepiness, or tiredness (84%), confusion or difficulty thinking clearly (75%), and memory problems (69%). For eight of 14 captured postictal symptoms, the most frequently reported symptom duration was <5 min. Mean postictal symptom burden score was correlated with patient reported quality of life and epilepsy-related disability measures. Sleep or rest, medication, and food or drinks were the most common alleviating factors. Lack of rest or sleep, and stress most often exacerbated postictal symptoms. This work contributes toward a better understanding of the postictal period and informs the development of future interventions to minimize the impact of the postictal period in epilepsy.

papers.title: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache.
papers.abstract: Cluster headache is a debilitating primary headache disorder. During active bouts, headache attacks occur daily and can last up to 3 h. Besides the excruciating pain, the disorder can greatly impact a patient's mental health, sleep, and life quality. The reoccurring attacks as well as sleep problems may lead to energy depletion and burnout symptoms, which can limit a person's ability to participate in society to the extent they would like to. Our aim was to investigate the extent of burnout symptoms in a Swedish cluster headache cohort using a cross-sectional approach. We further wanted to study if burnout symptoms can be linked to disease status-and if sex, lifestyle factors, or any specific clinical characteristics may be linked to change in burnout symptoms. Between January 2024 and September 2025, the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire was sent out via the Research Electronic Data Capture platform to 839 study participants with cluster headache. Global scores from the questionnaire were compared between study participants in active bout and remission. Likewise, the scores were analyzed between participants whose remission period had lasted longer than 5 years (long-term) compared to less than 5 years (short-term). Lifestyle and clinical factors were further analyzed in study participants with high Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire scores (global score >3.75). The total number of individuals included in the analysis was 373/839 (44.5%). Scores above threshold (>3.75) were recorded in 65.9% (58/88) of study participants in an active bout compared to 37.5% (90/240) in the remission group (odds ratio [OR] = 3.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.93-5.38; p < 0.001). Participants in short-term remission similarly had a higher percentage of scores above threshold compared to participants in long-term remission (42.0% [73/174] vs. 22.2% [12/54], OR = 2.53, 95% CI = 1.25-5.14; p = 0.009). Participants with burnout scores above 3.75 were more likely to be females (OR = 3.25, 95% CI = 2.04-5.19; pcorrected <0.001) and report sleep deprivation as an attack trigger (OR = 2.24, 95% CI = 1.32-3.82; pcorrected = 0.034). Participants with cluster headache in our Swedish cohort reported higher scores for burnout symptoms, particularly during active bout. For participants in remission, the burnout symptoms score was inversely correlated to the number of years since their last active headache bout. When managing cluster headache in a clinical setting, it should be taken into consideration that this patient group has a substantial risk for developing burnout symptoms both in and out of an active bout. Future studies should evaluate how to best support patients with cluster headache handling exhaustion and promote recovery to improve their quality of life.

papers.title: Risk of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome by body mass index: Retrospective cohort study with Korean nationwide population-based cohort.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a gynecologic endocrine disorder affecting various aspects of women's health. Research examining the association between PCOS, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in Korean populations remains limited. We assessed OSA risk in Korean with PCOS, considering body mass index (BMI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study using health insurance claims data from the National Health Insurance Service. We selected 33 638 people with PCOS and 98 110 controls with available BMI data. This is a subgroup representing our previous retrospective cohort study, which identified the relationship between PCOS and several mental disorders. Hazard ratios (HR) for PCOS were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models. Obese individuals had a higher prevalence of OSA (0.60% in people with PCOS, 0.20% in controls) compared with the non-obese individuals (0.12% in people with PCOS, 0.13% in controls). PCOS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.483, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.029-2.137) and BMI (HR: 1.104, 95% CI: 1.069-1.141) were associated with an increased risk of OSA. Our findings suggest that the risk of OSA is higher in people with PCOS. This research holds significance by indicating that obesity at the time of PCOS diagnosis could serve as a potential predictor for OSA. This study supports international PCOS guidelines that recommend screening and managing OSA.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

papers.title: The Clinical Profile and Bedside Clues of Anti-LGI1 Encephalitis Presenting With Isolated Cognitive Impairment: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: A significant subset of anti-LGI1 encephalitis manifests initially with isolated cognitive impairment. Characterizing the clinical profile and bedside clues is critical for timely diagnosis and treatment. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 43 patients with isolated cognitive impairment during the first 2 weeks of illness. Patients were classified according to their entire disease course into sustained isolated impairment versus evolving neuropsychiatric syndrome. Domain-specific cognitive deficits (assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), paraclinical findings, and treatment response were systematically evaluated. Median age was 58 years and 67.4% were male. The MoCA revealed delayed recall impairment in 93.0%, with relatively preserved naming. Additional neuropsychiatric symptoms developed in 69.8% of patients, with median latencies as follows: psychiatric symptoms (21 days), FBDS (30 days), and focal seizures (47.5 days). The remaining 30.2% suffered from a sustained isolated cognitive impairment. The sustained-isolation subgroup was younger, had fewer naming deficits, and a similar immunotherapy response. EEG abnormalities (53.9%) and mesial temporal MRI hyperintensities (61.5%) were common in this subgroup. Isolated cognitive impairment frequently evolves into a broader neuropsychiatric syndrome, but a subset remains isolated. Delayed recall impairment with relative naming preservation, together with EEG and MRI findings, constitutes a practical bedside triad prompting early antibody screening and timely immunotherapy.

papers.title: A Pragmatic Approach for Brain-First and Body-First Classification in Parkinson's Disease: Insights from the Personalized Parkinson Project.
papers.abstract: The brain-first versus body-first framework in Parkinson's disease (PD) proposes distinct origins of α-synuclein pathology, resulting in discrete progression patterns. Although this pathophysiological distinction implies different clinical trajectories, feasible criteria to classify subjects in large cohorts are currently lacking. The goal was to develop a pragmatic approach for classifying brain-first and body-first PD clinical subtypes in a large early-PD cohort. We, therefore, explored a pragmatic approach to separating these subtypes based on motor asymmetry, rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, and orthostatic hypotension, applied in a large cohort of persons with early PD (disease duration <5 years). Individuals classified as probable brain-first were more often tremor-dominant and showed a trend toward less constipation, after adjusting for disease duration, age and sex. This framework enables subtyping in many existing cohorts, potentially advancing our understanding of PD pathophysiology and facilitating targeted therapies. Validation against gold-standard measures is recommended to refine these criteria further.

papers.title: Heteroatom effects on tricyclic fused aromatic molecules revealed by rotational spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: The gas-phase structures of dibenzothiophene, dibenzofuran, and carbazole provide detailed insights into how heteroatomic substitution changes the structural and electronic characteristics of tricyclic aromatic systems. Here we investigated the molecular properties such as rotational constants and the geometry of the three compounds in a supersonic expansion using high-resolution chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave (CP-FTMW) spectroscopy in a recently built spectrometer operating in the 2-18 GHz frequency range. Assisted by ab initio (MP2) and density functional theory (B3LYP-D3(BJ)) quantum-chemical calculations, the spectral analysis allowed us to assign the parent species and the heavy-atom isotopologues in natural abundance (13C and either 15N,34S, or 18O) for all three molecules. The isotopic data enabled the determination of the experimental structure through several methods, namely the substitution structure (rs), the vibrational ground-state geometry (r0), the semi-experimental equilibrium structure (rSEe), and the first-order mass-dependent r(1)m structure, through analysis of the changes in the principal moments of inertia induced by single-atom isotopic substitution. The experimental structures of these three heteroatom-containing PAHs are compared with the previously reported fluorene molecule. Finally, we discuss the underlying structural and electronic changes caused by the heteroatoms in the fluorene scaffold.

papers.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence links movement behaviors to vitamin D status. This study investigated associations between physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep with vitamin D status and explored sex differences in these relationships. This cross-sectional study included 3195 adults (49.1 ± 17.1 years, 45.5% males) from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete data. Self-reported PA, SB, and sleep duration were assessed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Generalized linear and logistic regression models were performed. SB was negatively associated with vitamin D levels in the whole sample (β = -0.006; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.012, -0.001) and males (β = -0.008; 95% CI: -0.014, -0.002), but not females. Sleep duration was positively associated with vitamin D among males only (β = 0.023; 95% CI: 0.003, 0.043). Meeting both PA and SB guidelines showed the strongest and most consistent association with vitamin D sufficiency, observed across the whole sample (odds ratio [OR] = 2.129; 95% CI: 1.504, 3.012), males (OR = 2.013; 95% CI: 1.021, 3.967), and females (OR = 2.214; 95% CI: 1.360, 3.605). Movement behaviors demonstrate independent and joint associations with vitamin D status in US adults, with modest sex-specific patterns that warrant replication. Combined adherence to PA and SB guidelines was consistently associated with greater odds of vitamin D sufficiency across sexes.

papers.title: Phenotypic and genetically predicted sleep traits in relation to dementia incidence in Swedish twins.
papers.abstract: Sleep and dementia are complex phenotypes shaped by genetic and environmental factors, but the genetic contribution of sleep to dementia risk remains unclear. This study examined associations of both phenotypic and genetically predicted sleep traits and their interaction with dementia risk. Data were drawn from the Screening Across the Lifespan Twin study (1998 to 2002) within the Swedish Twin Registry. Phenotypic sleep traits included sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, daytime sleepiness, chronotype, daytime napping, and a composite sleep score. Corresponding polygenic scores (PGSs) were derived from publicly available genome-wide association study summary statistics. Dementia diagnosis was obtained from national registers. Cox proportional hazards models estimated risk, excluding cases diagnosed within 10 years of baseline to reduce reverse causation. Among 13,087 individuals (mean age 70.27; 1541 dementia diagnosis cases), longer sleep duration (hazard ratio [HR] 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.86 to 1.00; p = 0.04) was associated with lower dementia risk over 13.42 years in models adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle behavioral factors. In within-pair analyses, this association was attenuated. Among 16,164 genotyped individuals (mean age 55.32; 559 cases), a one-standard deviation higher PGS for daytime napping (HR 1.12; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.23; p = 0.03) was associated with higher dementia risk over 16.01 years. In 3133 individuals with both data types (mean age 66.79 years; 377 cases), this association persisted independently of phenotypic napping (HR 1.17; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.33; p = 0.02), with no interaction observed. Genetic liability to daytime napping in midlife may reflect a distinct vulnerability for dementia, whereas napping in late-life may serve a compensatory or restorative function.

papers.title: Women with the FMR1 premutation: a within-family observational sibling study.
papers.abstract: Understanding the relative risk of the fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) premutation (PM) versus the risk of the PM and parenting a child with fragile X syndrome (FXS) is critical for PM carriers, their families and clinicians. For this study, we compared women with the PM with their biological sisters; some sisters also had the PM and some had normal-range cytosine-guanine-guanine (CGG) repeats. The sisters were further differentiated by whether they had a child with FXS. This study of 67 women from 30 families used multilevel modelling to probe the effects of the PM with or without parenting a child with FXS, with strong control for family-of-origin factors and background genetics. Controlling for the false discovery rate, we found that mothers with the PM who had children with FXS were similar to their sisters who had the PM but did not have a child with FXS in health, sleep, social relationships, depressive symptoms and executive functioning, differing only in anxiety and stress. However, there were many differences when mothers with the PM who had children with FXS were compared with their sisters with normal-range CGGs, including greater fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome-type, depressive and anxiety symptoms, poorer sleep, greater negative support and greater stress. In this study, the effect of the PM was stronger than the effect of parenting a child with FXS. Thus, the PM phenotype should not be primarily attributed to the effect of parenting a child with FXS. Additionally, by comparing mothers who had the PM and children with FXS with their sisters without the PM, the findings confirmed the effect of this dual vulnerability and here the vulnerability emerged even with strong familial controls.
